# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — breadth pass: 3 code fixes + 4 prompt rules across 5 failing clusters
- Changes I made (file/tool + cluster):
  1. tools.py `cancel_reservation` — in-body guard: raise if any flight.date < current date (cluster 3, task 37: extra wrong cancel of already-flown NQNU5R).
  2. tools.py `book_reservation` — payment auto-resolve: single method → set to total; one credit card among several → absorbs remainder; re-sync payment_history; else actionable error (cluster 1, tasks 25/8: payment-sum stall).
  3. tools.py NEW `list_reservations(user_id)` — loop tool returning per-reservation route/date/cabin/pax summaries (cluster 2, tasks 17/22: wrong reservation selected).
  4. policy.md "How to execute write actions" — confirm once → next output MUST be the write call; retry in-turn on fixable errors; never claim success without a returned call; 2 worked examples (cluster 1, tasks 8/25/40).
  5. policy.md "Finding the right reservation" — use list_reservations + match by route, never assume first (cluster 2).
  6. policy.md "Change passengers" — pass FULL passenger list after get_reservation_details (cluster 4, task 40).
  7. policy.md Modify→Payment — report exact charge/refund from payment_history newest entry, not a search estimate (cluster 5, task 11).
- Expected effect + why safe: each edit targets a currently-failing write. All are bounded — the cancel guard fires only on past-dated flights, the payment auto-resolve only on a sum mismatch, list_reservations is additive read-only, and the prompt rules are additive (loosen no deny/refuse rule). The one passing task (12) is a baggage update with a reservation id supplied and confirmed-once-then-acted; no passing task books, cancels, or does route-lookup, so passing behavior is unchanged.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — first iteration; LEDGER/JOURNAL/RUNMAP/prior_iterations all empty.
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet (no prior RESULTs).
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: task 19 (should-cancel basic-economy — trigger not safely determinable from the trace; a global rule would be an unbounded decision change). Task 23 is infra noise (max_steps null).
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration). If this iteration's RESULT is flat, the next lever to try is inspecting the eval task-DB states directly (this run's local base DB differs from eval), and designing the task-19 cancel trigger from flight statuses rather than prose.
- Focus next iteration: read this entry's RESULT line; keep whatever it marks fixed, redesign whatever it marks broke, then crack task 19 and re-examine any COMMUNICATE-only failures.
